problem:
Let $l=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ x \\ 2 \\ x \\ 2x\end{aligned}]$ and $m=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ x \\ 4 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$
If $l\cdot m=3$ and $x>3$, find the value of $x.$
worked_solution:
Starting from the equation $l\cdot m=3,$ we compute the dot product in terms of $x$ and then solve for $x$ in the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}l\cdot m & =3 \\ 5\cdot 1+x\cdot x+2\cdot 4+x\cdot (-1)+2x\cdot (-3) & =3 \\ 5+{x}^{2}+8-x-6x & =3 \\ {x}^{2}-7x+13 & =3 \\ {x}^{2}-7x+10 & =0 \\ (x-5)(x-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We get two solutions, ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=2.$ Since we need $x>3$, our final answer is $x=5$ only.
